passage:
The following text is from Kate Chopin's 1894 short story “The Story of an Hour.” Mrs. Mallard has just learned that her husband has died.

She could see in the open square before her house the tops of trees that were all aquiver with the new spring life. The delicious breath of rain was in the air. In the street below a peddler was crying his wares. The notes of a distant song which some one was singing reached her faintly, and countless sparrows were twittering in the eaves.
stem: Which choice best describes the function of the text in the story?
choices: It surrounds Mrs. Mallard with images of renewal that hint at an unexpected feeling of freedom.
It shows that Mrs. Mallard is too distracted by noise to understand the news she received.
It establishes that Mrs. Mallard's house is located in a busy commercial district of the city.
It suggests that Mrs. Mallard's neighbors are celebrating because of her husband's death.
steps: Right after news of a death, the scene is full of spring life, fresh rain, song and birds.
That contrast with expected grief hints at a feeling of renewal or freedom.
Nothing shows distraction, a focus on the neighborhood itself, or neighbors celebrating.
key: When setting details contrast with the situation, ask what feeling they suggest.
